problem: Opening a corpus-origin leaf FIFO for reading blocked before the existing regular-file validation when no writer was connected.
change: Open the leaf with O_NONBLOCK before fstat. Preserve no-follow directory traversal, regular-file refusal, bounded byte read and conservative origin classification.

predecessor.failure: No-writer FIFO exceeded five-second child-process timeout; other four methods passed.

test_scope: Five new actual filesystem subprocess controls plus four unchanged original CorpusOriginLabels methods. FIFO with and without peer; non-consumption; descriptor counts; directory and symlink refusal; regular-file origins.
execution: Read-only source/root; private tmp/home/run/dev/proc; unshared network/PID namespaces; 60s timeout and 5s kill grace. Explicit isolated test-home bootstrap. Each new child uses -I -B and a five-second timeout. No installed state writes.

static.comparison: Same rules, messages, columns and exact affected source lines; no new diagnostic signatures.

review.result: No blocker for narrow repair checkpoint

limits: O_NONBLOCK does not establish bounded regular-file or storage latency.
This reproduces one possible hang, not the historical installed recall timeout.
No installed recall, indexing, whole-system proof, static compliance or release acceptance.
Original assurance, recovery, continuity and release gates remain open.
